For derivatives the period-independent bound is the finite sum of eγ|z|1 times the absolute stencil coefficients over all orientations and stencil sites. Transposition preserves this bound. Composition of two rows with an intermediate orientation space of size n costs at most n times the product of their entrywise weighted bounds, by the distance triangle inequality and absolute convergence.
